subject: Archaeology
title: Port Royal: The Sunken Pirate Capital
description: A short lesson to help you apply Port Royal: The Sunken Pirate Capital.

hook.text: Jamaica's pirate capital sank in 1692 when an earthquake liquefied the sand beneath it. Two-thirds vanished in minutes.

buildup.text: Port Royal was the richest and most notorious city in the Caribbean — a haven for buccaneers and rum traders.

discovery.text: Underwater excavations found a stopped watch, tavern signs, pewter plates, and a chest of pirate coins.

twist.text: The liquefaction swallowed buildings whole. Some structures sank vertically with furniture still inside the rooms.

climax.text: Port Royal is one of the best-preserved underwater urban sites. The mud sealed everything like a time capsule.

punchline.text: Earthquakes turned sand to liquid and swallowed a pirate city whole.

quiz.question: How were Port Royal's buildings so well preserved underwater?
options: Coral grew over the structures and protected them
Buildings sank vertically in liquefied sand, and mud sealed them like a time capsule
Cold Caribbean currents prevented decay of organic materials

details.summary: Port Royal, Jamaica, was the wealthiest and most notorious city in the Caribbean until a 1692 earthquake sent two-thirds of it sliding into the sea. Underwater excavations have uncovered intact buildings, taverns, workshops, and personal possessions from the golden age of Caribbean piracy.
details.whyItMatters: Port Royal is a Caribbean Pompeii — a city frozen at the moment of catastrophe. It preserves 17th-century colonial life in extraordinary detail, from pirate taverns to merchant warehouses, beneath the waters of Kingston harbour.
takeaways: A 1692 earthquake sank two-thirds of Port Royal into the sea
It was the wealthiest Caribbean city during the pirate era
Underwater excavations reveal 17th-century colonial life in detail

faq.question: Why was Port Royal called the wickedest city on Earth?
faq.answer: Port Royal was the main base for English-licensed pirates (privateers) raiding Spanish shipping. Its wealth from plunder supported hundreds of taverns, gambling houses, and brothels. Contemporary accounts describe extreme debauchery, though these were partly English propaganda.

faq.question: What has been found underwater at Port Royal?
faq.answer: Intact building foundations, a pewter dinner service frozen mid-meal, a pocket watch stopped at 11:43 (the earthquake time), pirate-era tavern equipment, merchant goods, and thousands of artifacts spanning daily colonial life. The site preservation rivals Pompeii in some areas.
